blocks.text: Nobody has measured how investor relations officers split their working day. No study I could open tracks IRO hours by task. So the picture here comes from job postings, a 2024 survey of IR careers and general research on knowledge workers. Read it as a set of signals, not a timesheet. Your own week will look different, and that is the point of checking it.
Where an investor relations officer's day goes

A NIRI job posting for a Director, Investor Relations shows the recurring work in plain terms. The role runs the administrative calendar for quarterly earnings and investor conferences. It publishes earnings releases, presentations, webcast links, replays, transcripts and SEC filings to the IR website. It also keeps investor and analyst contacts, meeting histories and targeting lists up to date. Those tasks repeat every quarter, whatever the market is doing.

items: Earnings calendar: dates, dial-ins, rehearsals and conference bookings.
Publishing: releases, decks, webcast links, replays and transcripts to the IR website.
Investor records: analyst contacts, meeting notes and targeting lists.
Disclosure review: checking that each outside answer matches what is already public.
Platform upkeep: the posting names Capital Access, AlphaSense, Bloomberg and IDX.

blocks.text: The 2024 NIRI and Korn Ferry survey shows how wide the job has grown. It drew 429 responses between May and July 2024. Nearly 80% of respondents manage responsibilities beyond IR, up from 62% in 2022. 20% say competitive intelligence is part of their role, and another 20% say ESG or sustainability is. And 69% report to the CFO. The survey does not report hours, so it shows scope, not time.
Email, chat and interruptions eat the rest

Microsoft's 2025 Work Trend Index says the most active users, the top 20% by ping volume, get interrupted about every 2 minutes during the 9-to-5. Those interruptions come from meetings, emails and pings. The figure does not measure IROs. Still, anyone who runs an IR inbox will know the feeling. A draft stops, then restarts, then stops again.

The same report says chats sent outside the 9-to-5 workday are up 15% year over year. The average is 58 messages per user before or after hours. And 60% of meetings are ad hoc rather than scheduled. Those are knowledge-worker figures, not IR figures. They still describe the inbox you open first thing and close last thing.

Asana's Anatomy of Work report says knowledge workers spend almost two-thirds of their time on what it calls work about work. That figure comes from 2020 data in the 2021 edition, across knowledge workers in general. Use it as a ceiling check for your own week. It is not a measure of IR time.

blocks.text: Regulation FD: where an AI assistant helps and where it stops

Regulation FD covers selective disclosure, which means sharing material information with some people but not the public. Under the SEC's final rule, a disclosure is intentional when the speaker knows, or is reckless in not knowing, that the information is both material and nonpublic. For intentional disclosures, public disclosure must be simultaneous. That leaves no room for a slow reply.

Non-intentional selective disclosures have a looser clock. The outer boundary for prompt public disclosure is the later of 24 hours or the start of the next day's NYSE trading. The clock starts when a senior official learns of the disclosure. A slow review can run that clock down, so flag questions early. Do not sit on them.

blocks.title: Keep nonpublic information out of prompts
blocks.text: Do not paste material nonpublic information into an AI prompt unless your company's policy allows it. Lazur sends audio and the screenshot to AI providers to answer. Those are not stored, and content is never used to train AI models. Your policy still decides what goes on screen.

NIRI's posting for the same role expects AI and automation tools to be used with human review for sensitive information. That is a good test to borrow. The tool drafts and explains. A person checks the facts, judges the disclosure risk and presses send.
A check before any outside answer goes out

items: Is the answer already in a filing, release, webcast or transcript?
Does it confirm, deny or hint at a number that is not public yet?
Has counsel or the disclosure committee seen this type of question before?
If any answer is no or unsure, hold the reply and escalate it.
Ask Lazur to draft the escalation note, then send it to your IR lead.

blocks.text: Drafting analyst replies and talking points in Outlook

Outlook is where most of this work lands. Say an analyst emails the morning after the call and asks whether the margin range still holds. Start by asking Lazur to explain the question. It will tell you what the analyst wants, and where the question sits in the email. Only then ask for a draft.

A holding reply might say the company will not update its outlook outside its scheduled disclosures. Use that wording only if it matches your policy. Then work the draft in three passes. Delete any sentence that adds a fact. Check every number against a public source. Read the rest aloud, or ask Lazur to explain any sentence you doubt.
Dictation for call notes, CRM updates and board memos

Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. It saves the most typing on a heavy day. Use it for call notes, CRM entries and the short memo you send to the CFO after an investor meeting. Click into the field first, so the text lands where you expect.

Two features help most with IR vocabulary. A personal dictionary holds analyst names, firm names and product lines that speech tools often mangle. Snippets hold boilerplate such as approved wording, so you do not retype it. Have counsel approve any snippet that contains forward-looking language, and review it each quarter.
Building the earnings calendar in Outlook

The calendar is the most fixed part of the job, and the easiest to get wrong. Outlook for Mac 16.114, released October 14, 2026, added a choice of third-party online meeting providers when you create a calendar event. That matters if your webcast runs on a provider other than the default.

Keep one calendar entry for every step. Put the call, the rehearsal, the dial-in test and the replay check on the calendar. Then ask Lazur to create each event by voice. Check the time zone on every one, since analysts dial in from several regions. A wrong zone is an easy mistake on a list like this.
Excel and PowerPoint: checking the numbers before the deck goes out

Start with the version. In Excel, open Excel > About Excel and compare the number with Microsoft's release notes. Microsoft lists Version 16.114.3 (Build 26102720), released October 27, 2026. That build fixes an earlier update that disabled Office 2021 for existing users. If your build is older, update before the quarter closes.

Decks drift. A number changes in the release, then nobody updates slide 14. The Excel model is the source, and the slides are copies. Trace each copy back to the model, then to the release. The [Excel guide for IROs](/for/investor-relations-officers/excel) and the [PowerPoint guide for IROs](/for/investor-relations-officers/powerpoint) walk through the mechanics.

items: Pick the three numbers that matter most, such as revenue, margin and guidance.
Trace each one to its source cell in Excel, then to the release text.
Ask Lazur to point at every slide that shows the same figure.
Save a dated copy with File > Save As before anyone else opens the deck.

blocks.text: Legacy Outlook is ending, so check your version first

Microsoft's Outlook for Mac page says the new Outlook is opt-in. You turn off the Legacy Outlook switch to move across. The same page says support for legacy Outlook for Mac ends in October 2026. Continued support depends on your Microsoft 365, Office or Outlook license.

SMU IT gives a sharper date. It says legacy Outlook on macOS stops working on October 1, 2026, when Microsoft retires the protocol that legacy mode uses to reach Exchange Online. Microsoft has not confirmed that exact day. Today is November 9, 2026, so treat legacy Outlook as at risk. Ask your IT team which version you run.
Mistakes that waste the time you save

items: Asking for a full answer when you need a question. Ask Lazur to explain first, then draft.
Sending a draft straight out. Check it against the public record first.
Treating a spoken answer as legal advice. Lazur explains. Counsel decides.
Dictating into the wrong window. Click into the field before you hold fn.
Keeping old snippets. Approved wording changes, so review them each quarter.

blocks.text: The most expensive mistake is trusting an old number. The release changed, and the deck did not. Check the date on every source before you reuse it. A quick look at the timestamp beats a correction after the call.
A simple plan for your first two weeks

Start with one repeated task. Pick the reply you write most often, or the calendar you rebuild each quarter. Run that one task with Lazur for a week. Note where the voice requests help and where they slow you down. Then add the next task.

items: Get Lazur from the [download page](/download), then open it once on your Mac.
Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask where the next button is in a task you repeat.
Get a written AI rule for prompts with nonpublic information from your company.
Check the plan details on the [pricing page](/pricing) before you commit.
After one week, keep the requests that saved time and drop the rest.

faq.question: What is an AI assistant for investor relations?
faq.answer: It is a tool that helps an IR officer with daily work: drafting, explaining, finding things on screen and running research. Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. You hold a key and ask. It answers out loud, points at things, and types text when you ask. It does not click or send for you.

faq.question: Can an AI assistant write analyst replies for me?
faq.answer: It can draft one. Keep the draft to what is already public. Have your IR lead, counsel or disclosure committee check any answer that touches guidance, unreleased numbers or a question you have not seen before. Lazur drafts. You decide what goes out.

faq.question: Does Lazur work in Outlook and Excel on my Mac?
faq.answer: Lazur works in any app on your Mac, because it sees the screen while you hold the shortcut. Microsoft's release notes list Excel for Mac 16.114.3 and Outlook for Mac 16.114 as recent builds. Check your Excel version under Excel > About Excel.

faq.question: Is it safe to use AI with material nonpublic information?
faq.answer: Only if your company's policy allows it. The NIRI posting for an IR role expects AI tools to be used with human review for sensitive information. Lazur sends audio and the screenshot to AI providers to answer them, and those are not stored. Your policy still decides what you put on screen.

faq.question: Does Lazur replace platforms like Bloomberg or IDX?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for any app, and it has no partnership with any app maker. Check each vendor's own documentation for Mac support before you rely on a platform for your IR work.

faq.question: How does Regulation FD affect how fast I must respond?
faq.answer: Regulation FD sets timing for correcting a selective disclosure. An intentional one must go public at the same time. A non-intentional one must go public within the later of 24 hours or the next NYSE trading day, measured from when a senior official learns of it. Ask counsel how your policy applies.

faq.question: When does legacy Outlook for Mac stop working?
faq.answer: Microsoft says support for legacy Outlook for Mac ends in October 2026. SMU IT says legacy Outlook on macOS stops working on October 1, 2026, when Microsoft retires the Exchange connection protocol it uses. Microsoft has not confirmed that exact day. Check with your IT team today.

painPoints.title: Calendar and webcast logistics

painPoints.title: Every answer needs a disclosure check

painPoints.title: Numbers that drift between files
